Entry Folk Taboos and Talismans Talismans, salt, iron, bundles of grass, lintel marks and countless small taboos constitute the way ordinary people face the uncertain world. Bachelors may call it superstitious, and nobles may laugh and say nothing; but when their children have high fever, there are storms at sea, or they are walking alone late at night, many people will still follow it quietly. Altars, relics, and prophecies can unite people and give a political claim the appearance of irrefutability.

Bachelors may call it superstitious, and nobles may laugh and say nothing; but when their children have high fever, there are storms at sea, or they are walking alone late at night, many people will still follow it quietly. Some people use it as a talisman, while others use it as the name of fear; the same prayer may make people draw their swords or put them down.
